India's FCRA Amendment Bill Sparks Debate on Foreign Funding

India's Parliament is considering the Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Amendment Bill, 2026, which seeks to modify the existing Foreign Contribution (Regulation) Act, 2010, governing foreign donations. The bill has drawn criticism from some quarters, including a US lawmaker who called it an "attack against Christians," and the Assam Christian Forum, which stated it would severely impact institutions in remote areas reliant on foreign funds. The Indian government, through the Ministry of External Affairs, has responded by calling the US lawmaker's comments an "internal matter." Some outlets frame the debate as validating concerns about foreign funding and a potential "foreign hand," while others focus on explaining the bill's provisions and the government's stance.
